name: catalyst-host-vscode
displayName: Catalyst Studio — rules, journal and traceability for AI-assisted development
description: Catalyst Studio for catalyst-governed projects: the chain of rules, requirements and work, what waits for a decision, the journal with every change's diff, boards, traceability, and commands run with your agent after you confirm.

commands.title: Catalyst: Load Specific Kernel Version in Memory…
Catalyst: Set Up Catalyst in a Folder…
Catalyst: Open a User, Role or Group

catalyst.frameworkPath.description: Path to a local checkout of the catalyst framework repository (containing BOOTSTRAP.md), used by the install-offer when a workspace folder has no catalyst deployment. Only needed if the framework repo isn't cloned as a sibling of your project.

catalyst.moduleSourceUrl.description: Source location URL for downloading Catalyst process modules. Supports Git SSH URLs (git@github.com:owner/repo.git/path/), GitHub tree URLs (https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path), standard VCS URIs (git+https://github.com/owner/repo.git#branch:path), or raw GitHub HTTP URLs.

catalyst.kernelSourceUrl.description: Source location URL for downloading Catalyst kernel releases.

enumDescriptions: Each project's detail panels open as tabs in one editor group of their own.
Every project's detail panels share one single editor group.
catalyst.detailPanelGroups.description: Where entity detail panels open: at most one editor group per project (default), or one group for every project. A project's first panel opens beside the active editor; later ones join its group as tabs.

catalyst.ignoredFolders.description: Folders this workspace leaves out of catalyst — absolute paths, or paths relative to their workspace folder. No deployment is shown and no install is offered for them or anything below. To leave a folder out for everyone, commit an empty .catalystignore in it instead.

catalyst.trackEntityInTree.description: Select in the chain inspector the entity a detail panel shows — when it is opened from a link, or brought to the front. Only while the chain inspector is visible; it never opens the sidebar.

catalyst.iam.command.markdownDescription: The catalyst-users command line: the facade to whatever identity provider catalyst-users is configured for (its home, `~/.catalyst/users`), which signs in the account catalyst uses locally, on the system's behalf. The extension holds no credential. E.g. `uv run --project ~/sources/catalyst-users catalyst-users`. Run without a shell: its words are split on blanks, quotes keep a word together, and a leading `~/` is your home directory. [Check the account](command:catalyst.checkIamAccount).

scripts.prebuild: npm run build:webview --workspace=catalyst-ui && npm run build --workspace=catalyst-studio && mkdir -p dist && cp ../catalyst-ui/dist/webview.js dist/webview.js && rm -rf dist/studio && cp -R ../catalyst-studio/dist/web dist/studio
scripts.package: npm run build && npm run bundle && npx vsce package --no-dependencies -o catalyst-host-vscode.vsix
scripts.publish: npm run build && npm run bundle && npx vsce publish --no-dependencies

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace catalyst only reads: the chain inspector, details and diagnostics work; install and sync offers and agent commands wait until the workspace is trusted.

virtualWorkspaces.description: catalyst reads the deployment's working copy and runs its CLI and agent on a file system; a virtual workspace has none.
